acceptance_criteria.statement: WriteProposalWorkflow.handle remains the sole application-facing write Interface. Every pre-acquisition Workspace/resource/execution authorization, exact compatibility, complete m4r1 or proposal-expiry denial creates no execution/acquisition/admission/audit-start artifact and zero provider calls. Independently granted read-only or observation-only authority cannot escalate to execution/write authority.

The server-owned logical ID and canonical-json-v1 complete-intent fingerprint remain immutable. acquire_execution uses fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time and atomically commits one complete generation-1 AcquireWitness containing executing lifecycle/revision, owner/generation, database lease, authorized binding snapshot, proposal/logical ID/fingerprint and linked acquisition audit. Every identified concurrent loser makes zero gateway/provider calls and every pre-commit fault leaves no partial tuple.

A fixed global reference-key plus Workspace dispatch epoch vector serializes all supported authority/selector/key mutation adapters. After acquisition, authorize_and_admit_dispatch locks execution and both epochs, reloads all current facts and fully reverifies exact m4r1 canonical bytes, MAC, claims, trusted-store equality, key identity/status and expiry. Independent post-acquisition corruption/trusted-store/key/authority mutations deny with no admission or provider call.

Fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time and current owner/generation plus unexpired lease/reference atomically commit at most one immutable DispatchAdmissionWitness per logical execution. One private row binds every schema/purpose, Workspace/proposal/logical identity/fingerprint, exact capability/binding/policy/reference and complete-intent digest, authority decision/epoch witness, owner/generation, database times, non-secret signing provenance, opaque routing digest, exact envelope bytes/digest and linked audit field. Read-after-commit/restart compares the complete tuple; ambiguous commit reads it back byte-identically.

Admission commit is the logical start of the provider write. The exact privately persisted m4-dispatch-admission-v1 envelope is the only create_ticket input. After admission-first, later authority/selector/key mutation or proposal/reference/lease expiry cannot reauthorize, cancel, replace, upgrade or retarget the dispatch; the original byte-identical envelope/intent is sent exactly once. Mutation-first remains denied.

The SQLite reference-provider Adapter verifies envelope integrity and recomputed signed-intent fingerprint before its provider-owned logical-ID ledger. One BEGIN IMMEDIATE commits effect or closed rejection with outcome. Same ID/fingerprint replays; two independently valid test-harness envelopes with the same ID and different self-consistent fingerprints reach ProviderIdempotencyConflict before target lookup/mutation and create no second effect; tampering fails earlier.

Every post-admission crash/session/transport/ack uncertainty remains executing with the same outstanding admission/logical identity/fingerprint and typed indeterminate_external_outcome. A read-only provider contract-harness lookup before receipt yields provider_outcome_not_found and does not retire/finalize the admission or grant retry; direct target_not_found is a distinct ledgered terminal business rejection. #77 reloads NoAdmission or AdmissionOutstanding recovery seeds but performs no observation workflow, retry, replay, takeover, first-admission recovery or generation 2+.

record_execution_observation and finalize_execution use fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time and require current generation-1 owner and lease. Delayed success/closed failure across expiry is fenced with no observation/audit or terminal rewrite; provider truth remains independently observable.

Only direct success and target_not_found, validation_rejected or policy_rejected finalize; receipt-possible results remain executing/202 and provider fingerprint conflict remains executing/409 with no retry authority. Public projections are sanitized and observation/read authority never constructs write authority or an admission envelope.

A post-restart canonical append-only audit projection exactly reconstructs caller/proposal/approval/execution actors, both current decisions, compatibility, complete acquisition/admission witnesses, authority epochs, database times, provider alias, immutable intent/identity/fingerprint, observations and outcome while excluding raw provider IDs/routing, envelope bytes/MAC, keys, credentials and authority secrets. M1-M3 regressions remain green.

design_decisions.decision: Keep one deep ExecuteApprovedProposal application call. Acquisition, authorization, admission, dispatch, observation and finalization ordering remain hidden; witnesses are persistence/release evidence, not caller Interfaces.
Use durable PostgreSQL admission committed before provider I/O, never a live cross-store receipt guard. Post-admission uncertainty is receipt-possible and SQLite remains independent provider truth.
Persist the exact canonical envelope bytes in the one admission row with retained versioned verification material; no current selector/reference fact is read between admission commit and dispatch.

Use a provider-only contract harness with a non-runtime trusted signing Adapter to exercise the defensive same-ID/different-valid-fingerprint SQLite ledger path without exposing forging capability to application/HTTP composition.

Persist a read-only downstream ExecutionRecoverySeed as NoAdmission or AdmissionOutstanding. #77 tests only storage/reload and absence of recovery behavior; all provider-first reconciliation, takeover, retry and generation 2+ remain #78 acceptance.

Use fresh PostgreSQL clock_timestamp after blocking locks for #77 execution decisions, refining earlier transaction-start timestamp wording while preserving PostgreSQL time authority and the application Interface.

invariants: No gateway call exists without one durable admission; at most one admission exists per logical execution.
Every acquisition loser makes zero provider calls; provider idempotency cannot hide a losing workflow contender reaching the provider.
Every new admission is linearized with current authority, exact compatibility and full m4r1 verification under the fixed epoch vector.
Admission-first is an already-started write; later mutation or expiry cannot cancel or retarget its byte-identical envelope.
Provider effect and idempotency outcome commit atomically in provider-owned SQLite; ToolActionStore never invents provider truth.
Provider outcome not-found and terminal target_not_found are disjoint typed and persistence outcomes.
#77 creates and acts only on generation 1 and performs no reconciliation, retry, replay authorization, orphan recovery or takeover.
The compiled registry remains static and typed; no plugin/provider discovery framework is introduced.
Raw provider IDs/routing, envelope bytes/MAC, credentials, key material and authority secrets never enter audit/public projections.
out_of_scope: ReconcileExecution application flow, provider-first recovery orchestration, stale takeover, generation 2+, authorized replay, orphan first-admission recovery and stale-owner recovery, owned by #78.
A provider-atomic cancellation protocol, distributed transaction/rollback or arbitrary remote-vendor time protocol.
Dynamic plugins, capability discovery, runtime provider registration or a general marketplace.
Editing immutable proposals or silently reusing approval after material capability, binding, policy or reference change.
Final M4 fixed-point code review, forbidden until #75-#79 are accepted, integrated and closed.

test_cases.statement: At application and HTTP seams, independently deny every pre-acquisition class and Execute with principals proven to have only read, only observation, or both read/observation authority without execution authority.
test_cases.oracle: Each returns the exact denial with no execution/acquisition/admission/audit-start artifact and zero provider calls; presence of the limited grants is independently asserted.

test_cases.statement: Race identified public-workflow contenders and inject faults after each acquisition write before commit.
test_cases.oracle: One AcquireApplied contender owns one complete atomic tuple and is the only possible gateway caller; every loser has per-contender zero calls. Separate snapshots see no pre-commit partial state; rollback restores approved with no tuple; restart reconstructs every acquisition field.

test_cases.statement: After acquisition and while admission is blocked, independently exercise every real authority/selector mutation and non-runtime m4r1 canonical-byte/MAC/claims corruption, trusted-store delete/replace/mismatch and key revoke/unknown/rotate/unavailable fixture.
test_cases.oracle: Post-lock reload/reverification observes every class, persists no admission, makes zero gateway/provider calls and appends only sanitized pre-provider evidence.

test_cases.statement: Race every real typed mutation Adapter against admission, race same-generation issuers, and block acquisition/admission across proposal/reference/lease expiry under non-database clock skew.
test_cases.oracle: Mutation-first denies or admission-first binds the exact prior vector; one byte-identical admission exists. Fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time decides each expiry and a transaction-start clock cannot revive it.

test_cases.statement: Read the committed admission row/audit in one snapshot, compare every AC-04 field to authoritative inputs, restart PostgreSQL and rotate the active issuance key.
test_cases.oracle: One immutable complete row and linked audit exist; exact persisted envelope bytes reload unchanged, no field is sourced from current mutable state and no second admission appears.

test_cases.statement: Pause immediately after admission commit; independently mutate/revoke every authority/selector/key class and cross proposal/reference/lease expiry before resuming.
test_cases.oracle: Exactly one gateway call carries the original byte-identical envelope and intent with no reauthorization, cancellation, replacement, upgrade or retarget; later lease expiry may fence only Knora finalization.

test_cases.statement: In private provider contract composition, deliver same-ID/same-fingerprint replay, two independently valid self-consistent same-ID/different-fingerprint envelopes, and separate tampered/cross-bound envelopes.
test_cases.oracle: Equal fingerprint replays one effect; both valid unequal fingerprints pass integrity/recomputation and the second reaches provider ledger conflict before target lookup with no second effect; tampering fails before SQLite.

test_cases.statement: Fault after admission before gateway, before SQLite commit and after SQLite commit before acknowledgement; in the no-receipt window call only the read-only provider contract observer.
test_cases.oracle: Admission survives, provider has zero or one outcome, provider_outcome_not_found leaves the exact admission outstanding/non-terminal with no retry, and direct ledgered target_not_found remains a distinct closed failure.

test_cases.statement: After restart reload executing with no admission and executing with outstanding admission as the two exact ExecutionRecoverySeed variants, then call Execute again.
test_cases.oracle: Execute returns current ExecutionInProgress; #77 performs no provider observation, admission creation/replacement, dispatch/replay, retry authorization, takeover or generation increment in either branch.

test_cases.statement: Delay direct success and every closed failure across generation-1 lease expiry and exercise the full direct/indeterminate/conflict application and HTTP result matrix.
test_cases.oracle: Observation/finalization are post-lock database-time fenced; only allowed closed outcomes finalize, indeterminate remains executing/202 and provider conflict remains executing/409 with no retry authority.

test_cases.statement: Restart PostgreSQL and SQLite independently after direct, indeterminate, conflict and no-admission outcomes and reconstruct audit solely from append-only records.
test_cases.oracle: The full AC-10 projection matches proposal/acquisition/admission/provider evidence; provider ledger remains independent and every excluded raw/secret field is absent.

test_cases.statement: Run focused M4.3, full repository pytest, Ruff, Compose and clean Alembic verification on the exact candidate SHA.
test_cases.oracle: All candidate checks and M1-M3 regressions are green.

command_projections.statement: Clean PostgreSQL recreation and Alembic upgrade with pinned runtime.
Focused #77 and full repository pytest with worktree-pinned PYTHONPATH and sequential PostgreSQL execution.
Ruff and Docker Compose configuration verification.

required_evidence.statement: Per-contender acquisition results/call counts, pre-commit isolation, rollback absence and exact post-commit/restart AcquireWitness tuple.
Real mutation-adapter epoch traces, complete post-acquisition m4r1 failure matrix and fresh post-lock PostgreSQL expiry samples.
One complete admission-row witness, linked audit, exact persisted envelope bytes, key-rotation reload and admission-first non-cancellation traces.
Atomic SQLite effect/ledger rows, replay, two-valid-envelope conflict, tamper rejection and independent provider restart evidence.
Provider-outcome-not-found versus terminal target_not_found persistence/projection evidence and two-variant read-only recovery seed with absence of all #78 behavior in #77.
Sanitized public result matrix, exact full audit reconstruction, excluded-field proof, exact subject SHA and all governed verification totals/exits.

prior_findings.problem: V5 could pass while losers reached provider and did not compare the complete atomic acquisition tuple.
prior_findings.required_change: Correlate every contender, prove loser zero calls and compare pre-commit absence, rollback and full post-commit/restart tuple.

prior_findings.problem: V5 did not independently exercise every post-acquisition reference integrity/trust/key failure.
prior_findings.required_change: Add exact post-acquisition corruption, trusted-store and key fixtures and require post-lock denial with zero admission/calls.

prior_findings.problem: V5 did not compare every required admission field as one atomic row.
prior_findings.required_change: Persist/read one complete private row and compare every field plus linked audit before/after restart.

prior_findings.problem: V5 lacked an admission-first barrier proving later mutation/expiry cannot cancel or retarget.
prior_findings.required_change: Parameterize every later mutation/expiry and require the original byte-identical envelope exactly once without reauthorization.

prior_findings.problem: A changed fingerprint on the same envelope was invalid before the provider conflict path.
prior_findings.required_change: Use two independently valid non-runtime test envelopes for the same ID/different self-consistent fingerprints and prove provider ledger conflict.

prior_findings.problem: V5 placed future #78 runtime behavior inside #77 acceptance.
prior_findings.required_change: Limit #77 acceptance to read-only recovery seed persistence/reload and prove absence of recovery/retry/takeover behavior; move runtime rules to downstream dependency contract.

prior_findings.problem: V5 did not observe provider-ledger not-found or distinguish it from direct target_not_found.
prior_findings.required_change: Use a read-only provider contract lookup in the no-receipt window and compare its non-terminal persistence with separate ledgered target_not_found.

prior_findings.problem: V5 generic denial did not prove limited grants cannot escalate to write.
prior_findings.required_change: Independently establish read/observation-only grants then Execute and prove pre-acquisition denial/no state/no calls at application and HTTP seams.

prior_findings.problem: V4 incorrectly relied on live PostgreSQL guard loss as proof-no-write across SQLite.
prior_findings.required_change: Persist admission before I/O and classify every post-admission session/crash uncertainty as receipt-possible without cross-store rollback claims.

prior_findings.problem: Earlier revisions raced only one revocation class.
prior_findings.required_change: Race every real authority/selector/reference-key mutation Adapter under a fixed ownership/lock map.

prior_findings.problem: Earlier admission issuance did not prove time sampled after blocking locks.
prior_findings.required_change: Block acquisition/admission across exact expiry boundaries and require fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time under skewed other clocks.

prior_findings.problem: Earlier tests did not directly fence both observation and finalization across lease expiry.
prior_findings.required_change: Parameterize both operations across expiry and prove no observation/audit or terminal rewrite.

prior_findings.problem: Earlier #77 acceptance leaked a generation-change/takeover fixture.
prior_findings.required_change: Use only generation-1 persistence/fencing and explicitly prove no takeover/generation increment; retain runtime recovery for #78.

prior_findings.problem: Earlier tests lacked a full public-workflow denial matrix.
prior_findings.required_change: Cover every denial class with no execution/admission/audit-start and zero calls.

prior_findings.problem: Earlier restart evidence did not compare every required audit field.
prior_findings.required_change: Reconstruct and compare the complete canonical projection solely from append-only records and prove excluded fields absent.
